text:
Nick Schmaltz left the Nov. 11 loss in Vegas after 7:19 with what RotoBaller and others reported as a lower-body injury, and RotoWire had him out Thursday. For a Mammoth team already short on bodies, that's a real hole, because Schmaltz has been their power play's brain: 13 of his 20 points have come with the man advantage.

The rest of the picture is more complicated. At five on five, Utah has had only 44.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 16 points worse than when he sits. Some of that is bad luck: his team has scored 6.6 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him out there, which usually swings back. His own shooting, 19.1% against a career-like 15%, probably swings the other way.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 91st percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season. When he's back, watch whether the even-strength chances return with him.
headline: Schmaltz is hurt, and Utah feels it
